message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 in European populations**

| Source | Population | Minor allele (C) frequency | Major allele (T) frequency |
|--------|------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **gnomAD v2.1.1** | Non‑Finnish European (NFE) | **≈ 0.12 (12 %)** | ≈ 0.88 (88 %) |
| **gnomAD v3.1.1** | European (EUR) | **≈ 0.11–0.13** | ≈ 0.87–0.89 |
| **1000 Genomes Project** | EUR (all sub‑populations combined) | **≈ 0.10–0.14** | ≈ 0.86–0.90 |

> **Interpretation**  
> The C allele of rs7412 corresponds to the APOE ε2 allele. In most European ancestry cohorts, the ε2 allele is present in roughly 10–15 % of chromosomes, with the remaining 85–90 % carrying the ε3 allele (T allele). The exact frequency can vary slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Northern vs. Southern Europe) but generally stays within this range.

### Key references

| Reference | Link |
|-----------|------|
| gnomAD v2.1.1 – Variant summary for rs7412 | <https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/rs7412> |
| gnomAD v3.1.1 – Variant summary for rs7412 | <https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/rs7412?dataset=gnomad_r3> |
| 1000 Genomes Project – Phase 3 variant data | <https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal> |

> **Note**  
> These frequencies are derived from large, publicly available datasets and represent the *minor allele frequency* (MAF) in the sampled populations. If you need a more precise estimate for a specific sub‑population or a different dataset, let me know and I can look up the exact numbers.
